questions.q: What is the programme mainly about?
options: How to stop your hair going grey as you get older
Human hair: why it matters and what it says about ageing
The best ways to cut and style hair for different faces
Why cats and gorillas have so much more hair than us
questions.why: Neil and Tim talk about hair, why it's important to us, and research into how hair follicles age.

questions.q: When do our hairs rise, according to Neil?
options: Only when we are angry
When we are hot and tired
When we see someone we don't like
When we are cold, scared or excited
questions.why: Neil says we get goose bumps when we're cold, scared or excited.

questions.q: What is Tim's theory about why humans lost most of their body hair?
options: It helped us sweat, so we could run and hunt longer
It helped us stay warm in the cold winter months
It made us look different from gorillas and other apes
It stopped insects and parasites living on our skin
questions.why: Tim says it let us sweat more easily, so we could run faster and longer and catch more animals.

questions.q: What does Neil say about men's and women's hair follicles?
options: Women have more than men
They have exactly the same number
Men have more than women
Men lose them all after 40
questions.why: Neil asks 'Did you know that men have more than women?'

questions.q: Why is a good head of hair important to people, according to Neil?
options: It shows health and youth
It keeps the head warm
It shows you are rich
It protects you from the sun
questions.why: Neil says 'a good head of hair indicates health and youth'.

questions.q: According to Ralf Paus, which hairs often get stronger as men get older?
options: The hair on the tops of their heads
Beards and moustaches on their faces
Eyebrows and hair in the nose and ears
Hair on their arms, legs and chest
questions.why: He says eyebrows and the hairs in your nose and ears get stronger in ageing men.

questions.q: Why does Ralf Paus think hair follicles are so interesting for science?
options: They could help cure baldness quickly and cheaply
They show scientists exactly how old a person is
They are the smallest organs in the human body
They might teach us how to stop other organs ageing
questions.why: He says 'we may even be able to learn from hair follicles how not to age'.

questions.q: How does Tim feel about hair follicles regenerating?
options: Very excited, because he thinks it will cure ageing
Unimpressed, unless it works for the hair on his head
Worried that it could be dangerous for older people
Surprised that scientists still know so little about it
questions.why: Tim says if it's only eyebrows, nose and ear hair, 'I am not that impressed!'
